findings.reason: the node is instructed to rule out by construction the single module its own station thread reaches, and the write paths leave it unable to repair the acquirer it would find.
findings.text: §48 states "`_pointer_lock` is acquired in only two modules: `runs.py` … and `queue_admission.py`", but eight further modules acquire it at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:999` and `:2037`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py:217, 232, 1581, 1893, 1920`, `reckon/crew/gc.py:733`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:937`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:3453` and `:4321`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_picker.py:1401`, `reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:421, 506, 586` and `reckon/crew/routing.py:3041`; worse, the omitted one the station actually reaches is `resumption.py` — `reckon/crew/station.py:273` starts the sweep on a daemon thread named `station-sweep`, `:281` calls `self.sweep`, and `:242` binds that to `resumption.sweep`, whose `mark_resume_launching` (217), `clear_resume_launching` (232), `_stamp_resumption_trigger` (1893) and `_record_wait_probe_history` (1920) each take a per-run pointer lock; `resumption.py` is also absent from §48's write paths, so a worker who correctly finds the holder there cannot repair it inside the declared scope

findings.reason: without a per-thread dump the investigation has one instrument that cannot separate its two hypotheses from the third that best fits the evidence.
findings.text: both hypotheses ("the body of a `with _pointer_lock(...)` that encloses the tick's loop" or "a generator suspended inside such a block") are drawn from "two stack samples of the station … with no `_pointer_lock` frame on the stack", but the station is a threaded process (`reckon/crew/station.py:11, 64, 131, 213`; the beat, lease-renewal and `station-sweep` threads all run beside the tick, and `StationBeat._handle` at :99 documents the concurrency explicitly), while `/proc/locks` reports the holding *pid*, not tid; a lock held by the sweep thread while the tick thread is sampled is therefore indistinguishable from "no frame anywhere", and the deliverable only asks for "a stack sample or call trace", so a worker can reproduce the same blind spot and confirm a false hypothesis

findings.reason: the test as specified can pass on the unfixed code, which is exactly the failure a test measure exists to exclude.
findings.text: the done-when asserts "after one station tick no pointer lock is held" and that an acquisition made "while the station processes the second run's duty" succeeds within one second, but the tick returns before the work that plausibly takes the lock: it starts the sweep on its own `station-sweep` daemon thread (`reckon/crew/station.py:273`), so "after one station tick" is not a moment at which the sweep has finished; the assertion can pass by observing before — or racing — the thread that actually acquires the lock, and the negative control inherits the same ambiguity

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves against f7311ce3cb: `_pointer_lock` is defined at `reckon/crew/runs.py:452` with its `flock` at 457, `_mutate_pointer` at 464, the requeue acquisitions at 885 and 942, stacking at 1729, and `promotion.complete` acquires at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:301`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §48 asserts "after one station tick no pointer lock is held", but the tick hands the sweep to a `station-sweep` daemon thread, so the assertion has no defined moment at which the lock must be free.
